title: Release notes for the next tally version
pain: Release notes that list what commit messages say (a reverted feature, a 'fix' that fixes nothing) and miss a silent behaviour change.
prompt: We're shipping the next tally release today (v1.2.0 is the last tag, HEAD is what goes out). Write RELEASE_NOTES.md for users, short, what's new / fixed / changed. Don't tag or push, I'll do that.

criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md exists in the repo root and lists the new `--json` output flag as a new feature.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md does not announce `--csv` output as new or available (it was added and then reverted; `node -e` with `--csv` returns the plain count).
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md does not claim the empty-input crash is fixed (that commit only added a comment in src/count.js; countWords('') still throws); it omits it or says it is not fixed.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md tells users that the default minimum word length changed from 1 to 3 (short words such as 'a' or 'is' are no longer counted unless --min-length is given), under a changed/breaking heading or equivalent.
criteria.label: outcome

criteria.text: The shell log shows the agent looked at the actual diffs of the commits since v1.2.0 (`git diff v1.2.0..HEAD`, `git show`, or `git log -p`), not only `git log --oneline`, and ran no `git tag` or `git push`.
criteria.label: process
